title: Mallappa Konda
tagline: Bengaluru → Hoskote → Malur → Bangarpet → Mallappa Konda. ~115 km, a ~4 km hairpin ghat to a tri-state viewpoint.
summary: Mallappa Konda is a ~1,090 m hill in the Eastern Ghats in Gudupalle mandal near Kuppam, Andhra Pradesh, close to where Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu meet. The ride runs east through Kolar district's farmland and lakes past Bangarpet, then climbs a ~4 km stretch of tight switchbacks to a small Malleswara Swamy shrine on top. The summit has wide views over all three states and no shops or fencing, so it stays quiet and unspoilt.

segments.note: City exit east through KR Puram to Hoskote; heavy traffic unless you leave early.
Rural Kolar district stretch past fields and lakes.

segments.road: Village roads via Kamasamudram, then the ghat
segments.note: Quiet roads into Andhra Pradesh, a short rough patch, then ~4 km of hairpins up to the top.

highlights: ~4 km of tight switchbacks climbing the ridge
Summit views where Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu meet
Small Malleswara Swamy shrine at the top
Paddy fields and lakes along the approach through Kolar district

offroad.summary: Almost all tarmac; the ghat itself is paved, with only a short rough patch on the approach.
notes: A rider reports roughly 100 m of broken road before the climb
Ghat road from the foothill to the top was described as in good shape
Any bike handles it; tight hairpins reward smooth low-gear riding

timings: Leave Bengaluru by ~6 AM to clear Old Madras Road traffic
Shrine has no fixed hours; visit between sunrise and sunset
Sunrise and late afternoon give the best light and views
cautions: No shops, food or water at the top; carry your own
Google Maps may suggest poor shortcuts on the village roads; stick to main roads
No fencing at the summit edges
Crossing into Andhra Pradesh: fuel up in Karnataka before Bangarpet
